pharm: Topical azole antifungal; inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, reducing ergosterol synthesis and disrupting the fungal cell membrane.
quick: Apply thin layer once daily to affected and surrounding area
No adequate human data; minimal systemic absorption
Unknown if excreted in milk; minimal systemic exposure
summary: Luliconazole Cream 1% is a topical azole antifungal for interdigital tinea pedis, tinea cruris, and tinea corporis caused by Trichophyton rubrum and Epidermophyton floccosum. It is for topical use only and not for ophthalmic, oral, or intravaginal use.
indications: Interdigital tinea pedis (T. rubrum, E. floccosum)

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer to affected area and ~1 inch of surrounding skin once daily
Apply a thin layer to affected area and ~1 inch of surrounding skin once daily
Apply a thin layer to affected area and ~1 inch of surrounding skin once daily

admin: For topical use only - not for ophthalmic, oral, or intravaginal use
Apply a thin layer to the affected area and about 1 inch of surrounding skin
Wash and dry hands after application (unless treating hands)
Complete the full course even if symptoms improve
Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes
moa: Luliconazole is an azole antifungal that inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (an enzyme in the ergosterol biosynthesis pathway). The resulting ergosterol depletion damages the fungal cell membrane, producing fungicidal/fungistatic activity against dermatophytes.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to luliconazole or any component of the cream
relative: Application to eyes, mouth, or vagina (not for such use)

preg: No adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; systemic absorption is minimal. Use only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether luliconazole is excreted in human milk after topical use; systemic exposure is minimal. Use caution.
renal: No dosage adjustment; negligible systemic absorption with topical use.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment; negligible systemic absorption with topical use.
monitoring: Observe for local irritation, burning, or sensitization
Reassess if no improvement after the treatment course
counsel: For external skin use only; avoid eyes, mouth, and vagina
Apply a thin layer once daily to the affected and surrounding skin
Complete the full course (1-2 weeks depending on site)
Report worsening redness, swelling, or oozing
Keep the affected area clean and dry
pk: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); do not freeze
pearls: Short courses: 1 week for tinea cruris/corporis, 2 weeks for interdigital tinea pedis
Apply to the lesion plus ~1 inch of surrounding skin
Active against T. rubrum and E. floccosum
missed: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered; if near the next dose, skip it. Resume the once-daily schedule. Do not double-apply.
overdose: Topical overdose is unlikely to cause systemic effects given minimal absorption. If accidentally ingested, provide supportive care.
